title: Designing Real-World Relationships
summary: Synthesize association, aggregation, composition, and inheritance to model complex real-world enterprise architectures.
learningObjectives: Translate messy real-world business requirements into precise OOP relationships
Combine Inheritance (Is-A), Aggregation (weak Has-A), and Composition (strong Has-A) into a cohesive domain model
Establish clear lifecycle boundaries and ownership hierarchies in multi-tier domains
Produce UML-aligned Java architectures ready for enterprise persistence and services
expectedOutcomes: You can analyze any business scenario and accurately identify which relationship applies to each entity pair
You can build clean multi-class architectures that avoid both monolithic inheritance and excessive coupling

activities.title: Practical Context: The Senior Architecture Decision Framework

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: Consider a major airline. A `Boeing787` IS-A `CommercialAirplane` (Inheritance). The airplane HAS engines and wings that were built with it and die with it (Composition). The airline aggregates Pilots and Flight Attendants who work for the airline but exist independently and transfer between planes (Aggregation). A Passenger buys a ticket to fly on a flight from London to New York (Association).
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: Every relationship type has its exact, irreplaceable role: Is-A defines the machine category; Composition builds the aircraft fuselage; Aggregation manages the flight crew; Association manages passenger travel.
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: Real-world systems flourish when you mix and match relationship types according to true domain ownership and lifecycle boundaries.

activities.content:
When architects translate business requirements into software, selecting the correct relationship model is crucial.

Choosing inheritance when composition is needed leads to fragile software. Choosing weak association when strong composition is needed leads to orphan objects and lifecycle leaks.

This decision framework provides clear engineering criteria to evaluate any real-world relationship.

activities.title: Designing Real-World Relationships: Decision Tree and Evaluation Criteria
Full Synthesis: University, Department, Course, Professor, and Student
activities.explanation: This architecture seamlessly incorporates: (1) Inheritance (Professor IS-A Person), (2) Aggregation (Department AGGREGATES Professor), (3) Composition (Department COMPOSES OfficeRoom), and (4) Association (Course ASSOCIATES with Professor).

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `Course` holds an association reference to the instructor `Professor`.

activities.title: Hospital Management Multi-Tier Architecture
activities.explanation: HospitalFacility composes HospitalWards, which compose MedicalBeds. Meanwhile, Nurses are aggregated by HospitalFacility, surviving any ward renovations.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `Nurse` objects are injected via `employNurse`, modeling aggregation.

questions.question: A Customer places an Order. The Order contains OrderItems. What are the relationships?
options: Customer AGGREGATES Order; Order COMPOSES OrderItems
Customer IS-A Order; Order IS-A OrderItems
Customer COMPOSES Order; Order AGGREGATES OrderItems
questions.explanation: Customer and Order have independent lifecycles (Customer aggregates/associates with Order), but an Order strictly composes its line items.

questions.question: A Dog has 4 Legs and is an Animal. What are the relationships?
options: Dog IS-A Animal; Dog HAS-A (composes) Legs
Dog HAS-A Animal; Dog IS-A Leg
Leg EXTENDS Dog; Dog EXTENDS Animal
questions.explanation: Dog is a specialized Animal (Is-A / inheritance), and Dog composes its biological limbs (Has-A / composition).

questions.question: Which relationship represents: 'A School has Classrooms (which cease to exist if the school building is demolished)'?
questions.explanation: Bound lifecycle and physical containment make School and Classrooms a classic composition relationship.

questions.question: Which relationship represents: 'A Company has Employees (who can leave and work elsewhere)'?
questions.explanation: Because Employees survive company closure and can transition elsewhere, it is Aggregation (weak Has-A).

questions.question: What is the primary danger of using Inheritance for every relationship in a large system?
options: Massive class explosion, fragile base classes, tight compile-time coupling, and violation of LSP
Stack memory exhaustion on every line
questions.explanation: Overusing inheritance produces rigid, brittle hierarchies that break when superclasses change.

questions.question: How do Aggregate Roots in Domain-Driven Design (DDD) relate to Composition?
questions.answer: An Aggregate Root acts as the top-level composite object controlling access to all inner composed entities.
options: The Aggregate Root is the outer composite object that guards invariants and lifecycle of its composed entities
The Aggregate Root is an abstract interface
The Aggregate Root must be static
It has no relation to OOP
questions.explanation: In DDD, an Aggregate Root encapsulates an entire boundary of composed entities, controlling transactions and access.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether a relationship is Aggregation or Composition, what question should you ask?
options: 'Does the child part survive when the parent container is deleted?'
'Is the child class public or private?'
'Does the class use ArrayList or LinkedList?'
questions.explanation: Lifecycle survival of the child object upon parent destruction is the definitive test.

questions.question: A Driver drives a RentalCar for 3 days. What relationship is this?
questions.explanation: The Driver temporarily uses the RentalCar; neither owns or is part of the other.

questions.question: In a clean architecture, where should persistence annotations (like @Entity) be placed?
options: On concrete Domain Entities that represent stateful database tables
questions.explanation: Domain entities representing tables hold ORM persistence annotations.

questions.question: What is the key benefit of modeling real-world domains with proper relationship semantics?
options: The code mirrors business reality, is easy to extend, test, and maintain, and minimizes unexpected bugs
questions.explanation: Accurate domain modeling creates intuitive, maintainable software that reflects actual business constraints.

questions.question: How would you model an E-Commerce system with Customer, Order, OrderItem, Product, and Payment in an interview?
questions.answer: 1. `Product` is a standalone entity. 2. `Customer` aggregates or associates with `Order`s. 3. `Order` strictly COMPOSES `OrderItem`s (an OrderItem only belongs to that order and dies with it). 4. `OrderItem` references a `Product` via Association. 5. `Order` associates with a `Payment` transaction object.
questions.expectedAnswer: 1. `Product` is a standalone entity. 2. `Customer` aggregates or associates with `Order`s. 3. `Order` strictly COMPOSES `OrderItem`s (an OrderItem only belongs to that order and dies with it). 4. `OrderItem` references a `Product` via Association. 5. `Order` associates with a `Payment` transaction object.
questions.keyTakeaway: Order composes OrderItems; OrderItem associates with Product; Customer aggregates Orders.
keyPoints: Order composes OrderItems; OrderItem associates with Product; Customer aggregates Orders.

questions.question: What is an Aggregate in Domain-Driven Design and how does it prevent data corruption?
questions.answer: An Aggregate is a cluster of domain objects treated as a single unit for data changes. External objects may only reference the Aggregate Root (e.g. `Order`), never its internal composed entities directly (e.g. `OrderItem`). All business rules and mutations pass through the root, ensuring invariants are always enforced.
questions.expectedAnswer: An Aggregate is a cluster of domain objects treated as a single unit for data changes. External objects may only reference the Aggregate Root (e.g. `Order`), never its internal composed entities directly (e.g. `OrderItem`). All business rules and mutations pass through the root, ensuring invariants are always enforced.
questions.keyTakeaway: Aggregate Roots encapsulate internal entities, preventing external tampering.
keyPoints: Aggregate Roots encapsulate internal entities, preventing external tampering.

questions.question: When modeling relationships in JPA/Hibernate, how do Cascading Types map to Aggregation vs Composition?
questions.answer: Composition maps to `CascadeType.ALL` with `orphanRemoval = true` (deleting the parent deletes all children). Aggregation maps to no cascading delete or `CascadeType.PERSIST`/`MERGE` only, ensuring children survive parent deletion.
questions.expectedAnswer: Composition maps to `CascadeType.ALL` with `orphanRemoval = true` (deleting the parent deletes all children). Aggregation maps to no cascading delete or `CascadeType.PERSIST`/`MERGE` only, ensuring children survive parent deletion.
questions.keyTakeaway: CascadeType.ALL + orphanRemoval = true represents strong Composition in JPA.
keyPoints: CascadeType.ALL + orphanRemoval = true represents strong Composition in JPA.

questions.question: How do you detect inappropriate relationship modeling during a code review?
questions.answer: Watch out for: (1) `extends` used purely to inherit helper methods, (2) leaking internal collections of a composite without defensive copies or unmodifiable views, (3) long getter navigation chains violating Demeter, and (4) bidirectional links that lack synchronization.
questions.expectedAnswer: Watch out for: (1) `extends` used purely to inherit helper methods, (2) leaking internal collections of a composite without defensive copies or unmodifiable views, (3) long getter navigation chains violating Demeter, and (4) bidirectional links that lack synchronization.
questions.keyTakeaway: Flag inappropriate extends, leaked collections, Demeter violations, and unsynced bidirectional links.
keyPoints: Flag inappropriate extends, leaked collections, Demeter violations, and unsynced bidirectional links.

questions.question: How does Polymorphism interact with Composition?
questions.answer: Polymorphism supercharges composition: when a composite holds an interface reference instead of a concrete class (e.g. `Car` holds `Engine` interface), any concrete implementation can be plugged in polymorphically at runtime, achieving maximum decoupling.
questions.expectedAnswer: Polymorphism supercharges composition: when a composite holds an interface reference instead of a concrete class (e.g. `Car` holds `Engine` interface), any concrete implementation can be plugged in polymorphically at runtime, achieving maximum decoupling.
questions.keyTakeaway: Composing interface references combines polymorphic dispatch with loose coupling.
keyPoints: Composing interface references combines polymorphic dispatch with loose coupling.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Value Object and an Entity in domain design?
questions.answer: An Entity has an ongoing identity across time and mutations (e.g. `User` with `userId`). A Value Object is defined entirely by its attributes with no conceptual identity, and is usually immutable (e.g. `Money($50, USD)`, `Address`). Value Objects are heavily used in composition.
questions.expectedAnswer: An Entity has an ongoing identity across time and mutations (e.g. `User` with `userId`). A Value Object is defined entirely by its attributes with no conceptual identity, and is usually immutable (e.g. `Money($50, USD)`, `Address`). Value Objects are heavily used in composition.
questions.keyTakeaway: Entities have identity; Value Objects are defined strictly by their attributes and are immutable.
keyPoints: Entities have identity; Value Objects are defined strictly by their attributes and are immutable.

activities.title: Designing Real-World Relationships Checklist
items: I can apply the master decision tree to pick the right OOP relationship.
I use inheritance only for true subtyping conforming to Liskov substitution.
I model shared or independent components using Aggregation.
I model exclusive, lifecycle-bound components using Composition.
I model temporary interactions between independent objects using Association.
I understand the Aggregate Root concept from Domain-Driven Design.
I configure JPA cascade types (orphanRemoval) to match Composition semantics.
I use immutable Value Objects for composed descriptive attributes.
I compose interface types to leverage runtime polymorphism.
I prevent encapsulation leaks in all multi-tier domain architectures.

practiceProblems.title: Vehicle Fleet Domain Modeling
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Complete the vehicle fleet model combining inheritance and composition:
1. Abstract class `Vehicle`: has `protected String vin`. Constructor initializes vin. Abstract method `public abstract String getType()`.
2. Class `DeliveryVan` extending `Vehicle`: has `private int capacityBoxes`. Constructor initializes vin and capacityBoxes. Overrides `getType()` returning `'Van (' + capacityBoxes + ' boxes)'`.
3. Class `FleetManager`: composes a `List<Vehicle> fleet = new ArrayList<>()`. Complete `addVehicle(Vehicle v)` and `printFleetReport()` to output each vehicle as `' * [' + vin + '] ' + getType()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
=== Fleet Roster ===
 * [1HGCR2F8] Van (120 boxes)
 * [1FTFW1ED] Van (250 boxes)
hints: Loop through fleet and call `v.getVin()` and `v.getType()`.

practiceProblems.title: Hospital Patient and Ward Multi-Relationship Architecture
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a hospital domain combining aggregation and composition from scratch:
1. Class `Doctor`: holds `private String name` and `private String specialty`. Constructor initializes both. Method `public String getBadge()` returns name + ' (' + specialty + ')'.
2. Class `Bed`: holds `private int bedNumber`. Constructor initializes bedNumber. Method `public int getBedNumber()` returns bedNumber.
3. Class `HospitalWard`: holds `private String wardName`, a composed `List<Bed> beds = new ArrayList<>()`, and an aggregated `Doctor supervisingDoctor`.
   - Constructor accepts `String wardName, int bedCount, Doctor doctor`. It instantiates `bedCount` new Bed objects (beds 1 to bedCount) internally (composition), and assigns the doctor (aggregation).
   - Method `public void printWardStatus()`: prints `'Ward: ' + wardName + ' | Beds: ' + beds.size() + ' | Supervising: ' + supervisingDoctor.getBadge()`.
4. In `Main`, create Doctor 'Dr. Gregory House' ('Diagnostics'). Create HospitalWard 'Ward-B', 6 beds, with Dr. House. Call `printWardStatus()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: Ward: Ward-B | Beds: 6 | Supervising: Dr. Gregory House (Diagnostics)
hints: Beds are instantiated internally in the loop (composition).
Doctor is passed in from outside (aggregation).

practiceProblems.title: E-Commerce Shopping Cart and Product Catalog Architecture
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build an e-commerce shopping model with accurate relationships from scratch:
1. Class `Product`: holds `private String id`, `private String title`, `private double price`. Constructor initializes all three. Getters for title and price.
2. Class `CartItem`: holds `private Product product` (Aggregation - product exists in catalog) and `private int quantity`. Method `public double getSubtotal()` returns `product.getPrice() * quantity`. Method `public String getLine()` returns `product.getTitle() + ' x' + quantity + ' = $' + getSubtotal()`.
3. Class `ShoppingCart`: holds composed `List<CartItem> items = new ArrayList<>()`.
   - Method `public void addItem(Product p, int qty)`: adds `new CartItem(p, qty)`.
   - Method `public double getTotal()`: sums all item subtotals.
   - Method `public void printSummary()`: prints `'=== Shopping Cart ==='`. Prints each item line as `' - ' + line`. Prints `'Total: $' + getTotal()`.
4. In `Main`, create Product p1 ('P1', 'Wireless Mouse', 25.0) and Product p2 ('P2', 'Mechanical Keyboard', 80.0). Add 2 mice and 1 keyboard to the cart. Call `printSummary()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
=== Shopping Cart ===
 - Wireless Mouse x2 = $50.0
 - Mechanical Keyboard x1 = $80.0
Total: $130.0
hints: CartItem aggregates Product instances (products survive cart emptying).

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Inverted Ownership in Company and Department Hierarchy
practiceProblems.problemStatement: A developer inverted the relationship in an enterprise model: they made `Department` compose the `Company`, so deleting a department destroys the whole corporation! Fix the architecture: make `Company` the container that composes `Department`s, and `Department` hold a simple name.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Company: Acme Corp
 - Dept: Finance
 - Dept: R&D
hints: Make Company the composite owner of Department.
Company.addDepartment creates new Department objects internally.

practiceProblems.title: Comprehensive Airline Flight Operations Hierarchy
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a complete airline flight operations domain synthesizing all OOP relationships from scratch:
1. Class `Pilot`: holds `private String licenseNumber` and `private String name`. Constructor initializes both. Method `public String getProfile()` returns `'Capt. ' + name + ' [License: ' + licenseNumber + ']'`.
2. Class `Passenger`: holds `private String ticketNum` and `private String name`. Constructor initializes both. Method `public String getTicket()` returns `'Tkt ' + ticketNum + ' (' + name + ')'`.
3. Class `CommercialFlight`: 
   - Holds `private String flightCode`
   - Aggregated `private Pilot pilot` (injected via constructor)
   - Associated `private List<Passenger> manifest = new ArrayList<>()`
   - Constructor accepts `String flightCode, Pilot pilot`.
   - Method `public void boardPassenger(Passenger p)` adds to manifest.
   - Method `public void dispatchFlight()`: prints `'=== Flight ' + flightCode + ' Dispatch ==='`. Prints `'Pilot in Command: ' + pilot.getProfile()`. Prints `'Passenger Manifest (' + manifest.size() + ' boarded):'`. Then prints each passenger indented with `' > ' + p.getTicket()`.
4. In `Main`, create Pilot 'P-8801' ('Chesley Sullenberger'). Create flight 'FLIGHT-1549' with the pilot. Board passengers: 'T-01' ('Alice'), 'T-02' ('Bob'). Call `dispatchFlight()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
=== Flight FLIGHT-1549 Dispatch ===
Pilot in Command: Capt. Chesley Sullenberger [License: P-8801]
Passenger Manifest (2 boarded):
 > Tkt T-01 (Alice)
 > Tkt T-02 (Bob)
hints: Pilot is aggregated by CommercialFlight (pilot exists independently of this flight).
Passengers are associated with CommercialFlight in the manifest.
